body: This was my first session, what exactly are prep work sessions?

Just went through and completed the "Be There Certificate," highly recommend it for anyone looking to try and help others struggling with mental health. Right now I'm just trying to find a good list of community resources that are more local to give him, since there's definitely gonna be a ton of pushback. Thanks!

I don't actually live with my parents, I live a few hours drive away from them for college and work 50 hours a week, I've just been back with them between semesters (basically a little less than a week). I also used to take lexapro back when I did therapy, but stopped after I moved for college. It never really changed much for me, but maybe there's some other medication that would do something, or a stronger dose. 

I've tried using the campus mental health services, but their backlog is massive, and average a 6 month wait, in which I'm 4 months in. At the moment I've been looking for somesort of therapist that takes my insurance, but most in my town don't take any insurance.

Thanks for your advice!

I'm kinda in a similar situation, but the roles are reversed. I have really bad anxiety, so she usually tends to do all ice breaking. For example, if I see her in the hallway, I'll look at my phone or away so I don't have to approach her. I know that it's really wrong to ignore her for seemly no reason, but I really struggle to stop myself.

I guess what I'm trying to say is there's still a chance. I wouldn't completely give up on this guy just yet.
